title: Gate context
description: Everything the gate needs, gathered by a platform adapter. Any CI can produce this file and run `aidd gate --context`.

platform.description: github, gitlab, local, or another adapter name.

trusted.description: False for local runs. An untrusted decision can never be posted as a status.

repo.description: The repository as the adapter names it (`owner/name` on GitHub, the project path on GitLab, the folder name locally). Reports and events show it; no rule reads it.

now.description: The time the gate runs, as an RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z. The emergency review window is measured from it; when absent, the gate uses the wall clock, so a conformance case always sets it.

id.description: The PR/MR number or iid, or locally the head ref. Recorded in the gate record; no rule reads it.

url.description: The PR/MR's web address, for links in reports.

author.description: Who opened the change: a platform login, or locally `email:<address>` from git's user.email. An author never approves their own change outside solo.

body.description: The PR/MR description, where the `yaml aidd` Change Request block lives (locally, a block naming the Spec the branch adds).

head_ref.description: The branch the change comes from: the PR/MR's head branch, or locally the branch checked out. The explore rule reads it: a `explore/` branch never merges as it is.

draft.description: True while the PR/MR is a draft; the draft rule keeps the gate pending until it is marked ready.

created_at.description: When the PR/MR was opened (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null. Anchors the emergency review window.

change.description: The change under review: a PR/MR, or locally the branch being gated.

head_pushed_at.description: When the head commit reached the platform (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null when unknown: a fact for the record's metrics, never for a rule. Locally, the head commit's committer date.

base_changed_at.description: When the change was last retargeted to another base branch (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), if ever. An approval given before it approved a different diff, so it no longer counts.

path.description: The repo-relative path at head (for a deletion, the path that was deleted).

previous_path.description: For a rename or copy, the path at base; null or absent otherwise. The scope and route rules check it as well as `path`, so a rename cannot move a file out of a protected path unseen.

additions.description: Lines added; counts toward the route's changed-line limit.

deletions.description: Lines deleted; counts toward the route's changed-line limit.

binary.description: True when the diff is binary; a changed-line limit cannot measure it.

added_lines.description: Optional: the lines the diff adds to this file, for the secrets rule, which warns on a line shaped like a secret. The local adapter passes them (at most 5000 per file, text files only); GitHub and GitLab do not, where the platform's own secret scanning is the control.

files.description: Every file the diff from base_sha to head_sha changes, one entry per path. The route, scope, and budget rules read it.

author.description: The commit author: a platform login, or `email:<address>` when the platform cannot map the email to an account (locally, always the email). Null when unknown.

committer.description: The committer, in the same form as `author`. A committer counts as an author: whoever committed a change cannot approve it. Null when unknown, or when it is the platform itself (list such accounts in `identities.system_accounts`).

message.description: The full commit message, whose `Assisted-by:` and `Co-authored-by:` trailers the provenance rule reads.

merge.description: True for merge commits, which need no provenance trailer.

verified.description: Platform-verified signature. Standard changes require true on every commit.

commits.description: Every commit between base_sha and head_sha. Their authors and committers are the change's authors, who cannot approve it outside solo, and their trailers are the provenance the gate checks.

state.description: The review's verdict. `changes_requested` from anyone whose approval the change needs blocks Merge approval; `commented` never clears an earlier verdict.

commit_sha.description: The commit the review was given on. Null when the platform does not say, and then the review is stale: only an approval that names the head commit counts.

submitted_at.description: When the review was submitted (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null. It orders the reviews; a null time sorts first and never passes a base change.

verified.description: Local-first only: true when the adapter verified the approval's git signature as good, from a key git trusts (with SSH signing, the Approver's own email principal). With platform `local` and `gates.local_approvals: signed`, an approval without `verified: true` does not count (`merge_approval.unsigned`). Platforms ignore it.

reviews.description: The platform's reviews on the change, in any order. The gate sorts them by `submitted_at` and keeps each user's latest that is not `commented`; an `approved` one counts only when it names the head commit. Locally, each `aidd approve merge` recorded on refs/aidd/decisions is an `approved` review.

body.description: The comment text. An approval command counts only on a line of its own, outside quotes, code blocks, and HTML comments.

created_at.description: When the comment was posted (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null; it orders the comments.

edited.description: True when the comment was edited after creation. Approval commands in edited comments never count.

verified.description: Local-first only: true when the adapter verified the approval's git signature, as for reviews. With platform `local` and `gates.local_approvals: signed`, an approval line without `verified: true` does not count (`spec_approval.unsigned`, `merge_approval.unsigned`). Platforms ignore it.

via_app.description: True when an App posted the comment for the person it names (GitHub's `performed_via_github_app`, a user-to-server token an agent may hold). Its approval lines never count (`spec_approval.via_app`, `merge_approval.via_app`).

comments.description: Comments on the change, where `/aidd approve-spec` (Spec approval) and, under solo, `/aidd approve` lines live. Locally, each approval line recorded on refs/aidd/decisions is a comment.

head_files.description: path -> text for the files the gate reads, such as the Spec.

base_config.description: Text of .aidd/config.yaml at base. Null when the base has none.

extends_texts.description: Pre-fetched parent configs keyed by path or url.

result.description: allow; deny; freeze (only route emergency passes); unbound (no command; fails on the routes in `gates.policy_required_routes`); unreachable (the command did not answer, which counts as deny).

detail.description: The command's own words, shown in the report.

rule.description: The org rule's name; it joins the decision as `policy:<rule>`, and its code is the same.

level.description: The level the Policy command chose for the finding.

message.description: What is wrong, for the report.

fix.description: How to satisfy it, for the report.

findings.description: Org rules the Policy command reported; they join the decision as policy:<rule>.

policy.description: The Policy command's answer, which the adapter runs in a checkout of the base branch. Absent or `unbound` when no command is bound; each finding joins the decision as `policy:<rule>`.

evidence.description: Evidence document, an invalid-artifact record, or null when no run exists for head yet.

commits_truncated.description: True when the platform returned only part of the commit list; authors cannot be verified.

notes.description: What the adapter wants a person to know, such as local approvals that did not count and why. The report shows each note; the decision never reads them.

org_preset.description: Text of an org preset injected by the gate as the implicit root parent of the repo config.

approvals_reset_on_push.description: Whether the platform removes approvals when commits are pushed (GitLab: `reset_approvals_on_push`), or null when unknown. False warns `merge_approval.survives_push`: GitLab's approval names no commit, so the gate binds it by time, and the platform's own approval count keeps an approval of an older head.

committer_approval_blocked.description: The platform itself stops commit authors from approving (GitLab: prevent approvals by users who add commits), so unlinked commit emails need no finding.

codeowners.description: The base branch's CODEOWNERS text, when the config reads it.

ancestor.description: Whether the commit is an ancestor of head.

paths.description: The paths the commit's own diff changes, from where it meets the base (`merge_base(base_sha, sha)..sha`); empty when the commit is unknown.

spec_hash.description: The Spec hash of the change's Spec as this commit holds it, or null when it holds none. A commit rebased away is no longer an ancestor; it still proves Spec approval when this hash is the Spec hash at head and its diff touched only the frozen files.

spec_hashes.description: For a goal's Specs: the Spec hash at this commit of each Spec its approval lines name, by Spec id (null when the commit holds no such Spec). One commit may be approved for several of a goal's Specs.

approval_commits.description: For each commit named in a Spec approval line: whether it is an ancestor of head, the paths its own diff changed, and the Spec's hash there. Proves Spec approval came before implementation, across a rebase too.

sha.description: The commit a revert commit's message names (`This reverts commit <sha>.`).

on_base.description: Whether that commit is merged on the base branch (an ancestor of `base_sha`).

exact.description: Whether the change's whole diff is exactly that commit's diff reversed, byte for byte apart from blob ids and hunk line numbers.

revert_of.description: Set when a commit on the change is a `git revert`: an exact revert of a merged commit may land on the emergency route with the incident commander's approval alone.

file.description: The manifest or lockfile, such as package.json, uv.lock, go.mod, or Cargo.lock.

name.description: The dependency, as the file names it; null when the file changed and no version could be read from it.

from.description: Its version at the base, or null when it was added.

to.description: Its version at head, or null when it was removed.

update_type.description: The first version number that grew; unknown (which counts as major) for an addition, a removal, a downgrade, or a version it cannot read.

dependency_updates.description: The dependency versions the diff's manifests and lockfiles move, which the adapter computes when the config has standard changes. A standard change's class allows only its `update_types`; absent means unknown, which counts as major.

dependencies_added.description: Every dependency a changed manifest declares at the head and not at the base, read by the adapter from the diff's manifests. A risk rule's `dependencies` match these; absent, no dependency raises the route.

name.description: The dependency's name as the manifest spells it.

content_matches.description: The risk rules with `content` that a line the diff adds matches, one item per rule and file, read by the adapter from the diff with the base config's rules. Absent, no content rule matches.

path.description: The file whose added line matched.

base_sha.description: Where that earlier head met the base branch (its merge-base with the base tip); null when the adapter does not have the commit.

identical_diff.description: Its diff from `base_sha` equals the head's diff from the change's `base_sha`, byte for byte, apart from the blob ids on `index` lines and the line numbers on hunk headers (whitespace, modes, and binary patches count; never the default `git patch-id`).

base_descends.description: The change's `base_sha` descends from that head's base on the base branch.

new_committers.description: Identities (`email:<address>`) that authored or committed the head's commits but none of that earlier head's: whoever rebased, when it was someone new.

approval_equivalents.description: For each earlier head an approval names: what the gate needs to decide whether a trivial rebase carries the approval to this head (`gates.approval_carry`). Absent or empty means no approval carries.

status_checks.description: State of each named CI check run on head: success, neutral, skipped, failure, cancelled, timed_out, action_required, pending, queued, in_progress, or missing.

sha.description: The commit the queue built for this entry and would move the base branch to: GitHub's merge-group commit, or GitLab's train commit. Evidence must be for this commit; `aidd/gate` is posted on it.

ref.description: The queue branch, such as `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-42-<sha>`, or GitLab's merge train ref, such as `refs/merge-requests/42/train`. For people; no rule reads it.

base_sha.description: The commit the entry was built on: the base branch tip, or the previous queue entry's commit. Evidence must have run against it.

stacked.description: True when `base_sha` is a previous queue entry rather than the base branch tip, so the entry also carries other pull requests' changes.

tree.description: The tree ID of the entry's commit.

merged_tree.description: The tree ID the adapter computed by merging the pull request's head (`head_sha`, the commit the approvals bind to) into `base_sha` (`git merge-tree --write-tree`), or null when that merge conflicts.

all_green.description: Whether the platform merges a group only when every entry passed its checks (GitHub: the merge queue rule's `grouping_strategy` is `ALLGREEN`; GitLab: always, since a merge train drops a failing entry and restarts the entries behind it); null when the adapter could not read it.

merge_queue.description: Set when the gate judges a merge queue entry instead of the pull request head: an entry in a GitHub merge queue, or in a GitLab merge train. Approvals stay bound to `head_sha`; the tests are re-run on `merge_queue.sha`, whose tree must be exactly `head_sha` merged into `merge_queue.base_sha`.
